statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r, the following holds. Define a value x to appear if there is some i with 0 <= i < n and (fronts[i] = x or backs[i] = x), and define x to be locked if there is some i with 0 <= i < n and fronts[i] = x and backs[i] = x. Let A be the set of all integers x that appear and are not locked. If A is nonempty, then r is the least integer in A: r is in A and r <= x for every x in A. If A is empty, then r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r (it does not fail).
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r, we have 0 <= r <= 2000.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r with r != 0, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < n such that fronts[i] = r or backs[i] = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r with r != 0, for every i with 0 <= i < n, it is not the case that both fronts[i] = r and backs[i] = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r with r != 0, there exists a set S of indices with S subset of {0,...,n-1} such that: (i) for some i in {0,...,n-1}, the down-facing value of card i under S is r, meaning fronts[i] = r if i is in S and backs[i] = r if i is not in S; and (ii) for every j in {0,...,n-1}, the up-facing value of card j under S is not r, meaning backs[j] != r if j is in S and fronts[j] != r if j is not in S.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r with r != 0, for every integer x with 1 <= x < r and every set S of indices with S subset of {0,...,n-1}, x is not good under S. That is, it is not the case that both (a) some card has x facing down under S and (b) no card has x facing up under S, where under S the up value of card i is backs[i] if i is in S and fronts[i] otherwise, and the down value is the other side.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no integer x and no set S of indices with S subset of {0,...,n-1} such that x is good under S, where under S the up value of card i is backs[i] if i is in S and fronts[i] otherwise, and x is good under S if x is the down value of some card and is not the up value of any card.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions and every index i with 0 <= i < n, let fronts' and backs' be the arrays obtained from fronts and backs by swapping the two entries of card i: fronts'[i] = backs[i], backs'[i] = fronts[i], and for every j with 0 <= j < n and j != i, fronts'[j] = fronts[j] and backs'[j] = backs[j]. Whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r and flipgame(fronts', backs') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions and every permutation p of the index set {0,...,n-1}, define fronts' and backs' by fronts'[i] = fronts[p(i)] and backs'[i] = backs[p(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < n. Whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r and flipgame(fronts', backs') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, whenever flipgame(fronts, backs) returns a result r, for every integer x with 1 <= x <= 2000, if x appears in fronts or backs and is not locked, then r != 0 and r <= x. Here x appears if there is i with 0 <= i < n and (fronts[i] = x or backs[i] = x), and x is locked if there is i with 0 <= i < n and fronts[i] = x and backs[i] = x.
preconditions: Let n = len(fronts). The inputs satisfy len(fronts) = len(backs), 1 <= n <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= fronts[i] <= 2000 and 1 <= backs[i] <= 2000.
